name: Activity tab counts
summary: activity(name, what, user): queries per day over ACTIVITY_DAYS ending at the snapshot day for an object, user, role, app (APP) or scope (OBJECT_NAME under name + '.'), totals by user/role/client/statement/object split into read/write/ddl, one row per user+role+client+object+statement+action with hours per UTC hour (weekdays), weekend and weekend_hours, first_day, kind and interactive; counts are per action, so a MERGE that reads and changes a table counts twice.

name: Activity hours in UTC, business time as an offset
summary: activity_sql groups per UTC day and keeps HOURS = {UTC hour: queries} (access.py:951-952, 970-975); activity() splits them into weekday hours and weekend_hours (access.py:4327-4330); the UI counts off-hours as weekend queries plus weekday hours outside [start, end) after shifting by a UTC offset (offOf, web/src/pages/Activity.tsx:25-26); default start-end from WORK_HOURS 7-19 (access.py:70, server.py:1674)

name: Activity view by object type
summary: activity_page picks the view from the object's kind: STREAMLIT -> app (rows where APP = name), DATABASE / SCHEMA -> scope (every object under the name), WAREHOUSE -> who ran queries on it from the usage read (warehouse_use, no ACCESS_HISTORY), else object; app and scope get no grant-path graph

name: Copy-only SQL behind the Activity tab
summary: query_sql(name, what, first, last): read-only SELECT over ACCESS_HISTORY x QUERY_HISTORY x SESSIONS listing every query id, time, user, role, statement, object and client in the window (no query text), filter per what (object, user, role, app by StreamlitName, scope by LIKE prefix), quotes doubled; the app never runs it

name: Grant path behind a use
summary: used_path(user, role, object, action): user -> shortest chain to the role used -> shortest data_use chain to a holder of a privilege that fits the action (READ_PRIVS for READ, else WRITE_PRIVS or OWNERSHIP) -> object; None when the role reaches no such grant now (admin role, grant gone).

name: Activity read window (incremental)
summary: Window = ACTIVITY_DAYS (60) back from now; rows of an earlier read are kept up to the day before its last day, and that day onwards is read again (ACCESS_HISTORY lags up to 3 hours). Same in SP_ACCESS_SNAPSHOT activity() (sql/1_setup.sql:586-594).

name: Rule 1: Technical role granted to a user or group role
summary: Technical role granted to a user or group role. Why: Technical roles belong under functional roles only. Severity Medium (access.py:131).

name: Rule 10: Person can write to a sensitive object
summary: Person can write to a sensitive object. Why: Writes to sensitive data should come from the build or a service user. Severity Medium (access.py:132).

name: Rule 11: Sensitive object reachable through a group role
summary: Sensitive object reachable through a group role. Why: Group membership is managed outside Snowflake, so reviews miss it. Severity Low (access.py:132).

name: Rule 12: Admin role is a user's default role
summary: Admin role is a user's default role. Why: Every session starts with admin rights. Severity High (access.py:132).

name: Rule 13: Orphan role: no users and no parent roles
summary: Orphan role: no users and no parent roles. Why: Unused roles hide access that nobody reviews. Severity Low (access.py:132).

name: Rule 14: f'Chain deeper than {MAX_DEPTH_RULE} roles'
summary: f'Chain deeper than {MAX_DEPTH_RULE} roles'. Why: Long chains are hard to review and hide where access comes from. Severity Low (access.py:132).

name: Rule 15: Future grant in a schema that holds sensitive data
summary: Future grant in a schema that holds sensitive data. Why: New tables there are readable before anyone classifies them. Severity Medium (access.py:132).

name: Rule 16: f'Dormant user (no login for {DORMANT_DAYS} days) still holds roles'
summary: f'Dormant user (no login for {DORMANT_DAYS} days) still holds roles'. Why: Unused accounts are an easy way in. Severity Medium (access.py:133).

name: Rule 17: Read-only role can write
summary: Read-only role can write. Why: The role name or its use says read-only, but it can change data. Severity High (access.py:133).

name: Rule 18: Unusual privilege set
summary: Unusual privilege set. Why: The role holds more or fewer privileges than its capability (READ, WRITE, ...) stands for, so its name no longer tells what it can do. Severity Low (access.py:133).

name: Rule 19: EXECUTE TASK held by a person or consumer role
summary: EXECUTE TASK held by a person or consumer role. Why: Running tasks belongs to the build or a service user. Severity Medium (access.py:133).

name: Rule 2: Direct privilege on a functional role
summary: Direct privilege on a functional role. Why: Privileges sit on technical roles, so the role model stays reviewable. Severity Medium (access.py:131).

name: Rule 20: OPERATE on a task outside owner/build roles
summary: OPERATE on a task outside owner/build roles. Why: The task runs with its owner's privileges, so whoever can start or resume it borrows them. Severity High (access.py:133).

name: Rule 21: Warehouse MODIFY or OPERATE outside owner/build roles
summary: Warehouse MODIFY or OPERATE outside owner/build roles. Why: Resizing, suspending or resuming a warehouse changes cost and availability for everyone. Severity Medium (access.py:133).

name: Rule 22: Stream on sensitive table readable without the table
summary: Stream on sensitive table readable without the table. Why: A stream returns the table's changed rows, so it leaks data its reader cannot read in the table. Severity High (access.py:133).

name: Rule 23: CREATE privilege on a schema held by a read-only role
summary: CREATE privilege on a schema held by a read-only role. Why: A read-only role that can create objects can copy data or change the schema. Severity High (access.py:134).

name: Rule 24: Person changed data or a table's definition
summary: Medium. A person (in USER, not a service user) ran WRITE or DDL on a known object with a role that has no OWNERSHIP reach on it (data_use(role)[1][object] lacks "own"); one finding per user and object: statement counts, the most used role, last day. access.py:5292-5302

name: Rule 25: Service user used from an interactive client
summary: High. A service user (is_service) has activity rows whose CLIENT is in INTERACTIVE (Snowflake UI, SnowSQL, Snowflake CLI); one finding per service user: queries per client label, tables, last day. access.py:5287-5288,5192-5198

name: Rule 26: Admin role used to read or change data
summary: High. Activity rows whose ROLE_NAME is in ADMIN on a known object; one finding per user and admin role: objects read, objects changed (action not READ), first three names. access.py:5289-5290,5199-5203

name: Rule 27: First access to a table in the last 7 days
summary: Low. Per user and object: the first day on the object is within the last NEW_DAYS (7) days of the snapshot and the user had activity before cut - NEW_DAYS (not a new user); detail adds "sensitive" for tagged objects. access.py:5281,5179-5183

name: Rule 28: Unusual volume on a table
summary: Medium. Per user and object with at least 5 active days: the busiest day has >= SPIKE[1] (50) queries and more than SPIKE[0] (3) x the median day. access.py:5308-5315

name: Rule 29: Streamlit app shows its owner's sensitive data to people who cannot read it
summary: High. Per Streamlit app (kinds STREAMLIT) whose owner roles (OWNERSHIP) read sensitive objects, per role holding USAGE on the app: users reaching that role who cannot read some of those objects through their own roles (user_reads) -> one finding on the holder role: app, owner, sensitive objects, users. Fix: revoke the app's USAGE from the role. access.py:4455-4470, app_exposure access.py:4415-4428

name: Rule 3: READ held directly and through another role
summary: READ held directly and through another role. Why: The direct grant is redundant and survives when the other one is removed. Severity Low (access.py:131).

name: Rule 4: OWNER role held by a consumer
summary: OWNER role held by a consumer. Why: Owners can drop and re-grant objects; only the build identity should own. Severity High (access.py:131).

name: Rule 5: Admin role held by a person
summary: Admin role held by a person. Why: Admin roles bypass the role model; use them through break-glass only. Severity High (access.py:131).

name: Rule 6: Sensitive column without a masking policy
summary: Sensitive column without a masking policy. Why: Everyone who can read the object sees the value in clear. Severity Medium (access.py:131).

name: Rule 7: Dormant or disabled person can read sensitive data
summary: Dormant or disabled person can read sensitive data. Why: Unused access to sensitive data is pure risk. Severity High (access.py:131).

name: Rule 8: Disabled user still holds roles
summary: Disabled user still holds roles. Why: Re-enabling the user brings all access back at once. Severity Low (access.py:131).

name: Rule 9: Privilege granted to PUBLIC
summary: Privilege granted to PUBLIC. Why: Every user, present and future, gets it. Severity High (access.py:132).
